output.brief: The August drop was mainly caused by the east-riser chiller failure. It ran from 4 to 19 August and left floors 6-8 at 26-29 C. Room comfort on those floors fell from 8.4 to 6.1. Floors 6-8 scored 6.8 for checkouts on 5-20 August and recovered to 8.4 once cooling returned. Of the 74 negative comments, 56 were about heat, and all 56 came from those floors. Cleanliness scores were flat. In-house inspection pass rates stayed at 95-96%. Check-in scores and kiosk complaints were flat. The survey method did not change. So don't serve notice on Orrin, and don't pull the kiosks. Neither is supported by the evidence. Don't exclude the floor 6-8 responses either, because that would hide a real service failure. The next step is to reinstate the deferred preventive maintenance on both chillers, hold critical spares on site, and write a guest-recovery protocol for cooling outages. All 517 affected stays already received an apology and a half-night credit, so any further return-stay offer is optional. The 6% rate rise may have added a little to the value-for-money dip on floors 1-5. That dip is within the usual August pattern, so I'd monitor it and not reverse the rise yet. I'm quite confident in the main finding and less sure about the rate effect.
